text:
maya: hi all, i'm on day 1 and trying to assume the redwood-prod cross-account role via AWS SSO but getting AccessDenied. command i ran: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RedwoodProdAccess --role-session-name maya-onboard` error: `An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the AssumeRole operation: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole` any idea what i'm missing?

cloud-onboard-bot: Welcome, maya! If you need production account access please file the Cloud Access form: https://go/redwood-cloud-access and include the exact AWS account ID + role arn. For immediate help, tag @eng-ops.

maya: filed the form this morning (ticket ONB-789) but wanted to try quickly. i'm logged in via Okta -> AWS SSO (Identity Center). my SSO user shows in the console but the CLI assume-role still fails.

devops-lee: quick checklist: 1) Confirm your AWS Identity Center assignment includes the target account and permission set that maps to the role. 2) If you're using the CLI with SSO, make sure you ran `aws sso login --profile redwood-prod`. 3) CLI profiles from SSO create temporary creds that should call AssumeRole on your behalf; if the permission set doesn't include sts:AssumeRole, you'll see that error.

maya: i did `aws sso login --profile redwood-prod` and `aws sts get-caller-identity` returns my SSO principal (arn:aws:sts::444455556666:assumed-role/AWSReservedSSO_RedwoodProdAdmins_abcdef123456/maya). but the role arn i'm trying to assume is in a different account (111122223333) where the trust policy might not allow my principal. how do i check the trust policy?

devops-lee: you can't view cross-account role trust unless you have iam:GetRole in the target account. ops can copy the trust policy for you. typically the trust policy should allow the SSO principal arn or the AWS SSO OIDC/SAML principal for your Identity Center. For cross-account via SSO we usually add "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::444455556666:saml-provider/Okta"} or a condition on `aws:PrincipalTag` depending on how the permission set is mapped. i'll pull the role trust now.

samir: fyi from security side: prod role access requires manager approval + short session duration (1 hour max) and session tags with `project` and `team` fields. make sure your cloud access form included the manager approval step or we hold the grant.

security-rachel: adding: we lock down the `sts:AssumeRole` trust to either the specific SSO permission set principal or require session tags to ensure attribute-based access. if the permission set was created without the right attribute mappings, the role will reject the assume. also check if the role requires `sts:TagSession` in the caller policy.

devops-lee: update: role trust currently allows the SSO-managed principal but expects session tags `team` and `env`. maya, when you run the assume via SSO profile the permission set must include `iam:PassRole`? not exactly  you need the permission set to allow `sts:TagSession` and the CLI to forward session tags. try: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RedwoodProdAccess --role-session-name maya-onboard --serial-number arn-of-mfa --token-code 123456` only if role expects MFA; otherwise use SSO flow.

maya: i don't have MFA prompt; Okta prompts at login. my permission set might be missing TagSession. where do i request that?

cloud-onboard-bot: To request CLI-enabled SSO permission set changes, update your Cloud Access form with "cli-sso-tags" and list required tags. Example note: `needs: sts:TagSession, session duration=3600, tags: team=platform, project=infra`.

devops-lee: i added a temporary allow for your SSO principal to assume the role for 2 hours while we fix the permission set (ONB-789 update). run `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile redwood-prod` then try the assume again.

maya: tried again and now `aws sts assume-role` works and returns credentials — thanks. terraform still fails later with `AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::444455556666:assumed-role/RedwoodProdAccess/maya-onboard is not authorized to perform: iam:CreateRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/infra-ci`. i think infra needs create-role privileges for the module.

samir: that CreateRole in prod definitely needs an exception. we usually avoid creating roles in prod from automation; prefer to create role templates and then operators apply them. for onboarding, we'll either grant a narrow `iam:CreateRole` with condition on role name prefix `onboard-*` or have ops pre-create the roles.

devops-lee: coming up with a safe option: ops can pre-create `infra-ci` role with the policy you need and add `trust` back to the SSO permission set. i'll make a ticket to pre-create the role and attach the policy.

security-rachel: approval note: manager must sign off before any iam:CreateRole in prod. rachel@redwood.com will comment on ONB-789 with explicit approval once the role template is attached.

maya: super helpful. i'll update ONB-789 with required policies and the terraform module path `infra/aws/ci`. thanks for the quick assist :thumbsup:

cloud-onboard-bot: After ops finishes role prep, remember to run `aws sts get-caller-identity` and `aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?starts_with(RoleName, `infra-`)]'` to confirm the new role exists.

devops-lee: note for future new hires: when requesting prod access via Cloud Access form include: account id, role arn (or permission set name), required session tags, required APIs/actions (e.g., iam:CreateRole), and business justification. saves time.

maya: noted, will include all that next time. thanks everyone!
